_comment: AI tool product data for AIfocus. Products support multi-category assignment via the 'categories' array. Scores use 3 dimensions (each 1-10): ease_of_use, academic_value, price_to_value. Overall is their simple average. affiliateSlug references data/affiliates.json entries. Optional displayPriority field (number, default 0) pins a product to the top of all sorted lists (homepage discovery, category groups, comparison tables, reviews index, schema.org ItemList). Higher displayPriority wins first; ties fall back to overallScore. Used to keep revenue-generating tools above non-monetisable ones.

products.name: ChatGPT Plus
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with GPT-3.5; Plus unlocks GPT-4
pros: Exceptional natural-language fluency across disciplines
Supports long-form academic drafts and outlines
Plugin ecosystem for citations and data analysis
Frequent model upgrades at no extra cost
cons: Can hallucinate references if not fact-checked
Limited real-time web access on free tier
products.verdict: The most versatile AI writing assistant for academics. GPT-4 quality justifies the subscription for researchers producing regular written output.

products.name: Consensus
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with 20 searches per month
pros: Searches across 200M+ peer-reviewed papers
AI-powered yes/no consensus indicators on research questions
Extracts key findings without reading full papers
Citation-ready output with DOI links
cons: Limited to English-language papers
No full-text PDF access — links to publisher
products.verdict: A game-changer for literature reviews. Consensus turns hours of database searching into minutes of evidence-based answers.

products.name: Midjourney
pros: Industry-leading image quality and coherence
Strong at scientific and technical illustration styles
Active community sharing prompts and techniques
Rapid iteration with variation and upscale tools
cons: Discord-only interface has a learning curve
Limited control over precise diagram layouts
products.verdict: The gold standard for AI image generation. Academics will find it invaluable for conference posters, presentation visuals, and conceptual illustrations.

products.name: GitHub Copilot
products.freeTierNote: Free for verified students and educators
products.useCase: Code completion, data scripts, analysis pipelines
pros: Inline code suggestions in VS Code, JetBrains, and Neovim
Excels at Python, R, and MATLAB — key academic languages
Free tier for students and educators via GitHub Education
Chat mode explains complex code and suggests refactors
cons: Suggestions occasionally introduce subtle bugs
Requires active internet connection
products.verdict: Essential for academics who write code. The free student tier and deep editor integration make it the easiest productivity win in research computing.

products.name: Elicit
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with 5,000 credits per month
products.useCase: Systematic reviews, paper discovery, data extraction
pros: Purpose-built for academic research workflows
Extracts structured data from papers automatically
Identifies methodological details across studies
Generous free tier for individual researchers
cons: Smaller paper index than Google Scholar
Export options limited on free plan
products.verdict: The most research-aware AI tool available. Elicit understands academic papers at a structural level that general-purpose chatbots cannot match.

products.name: Grammarly with AI
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with basic grammar and spelling checks
pros: Works inline across browsers, Word, and Google Docs
Academic tone detector helps match journal conventions
AI rewrite suggestions preserve original meaning
Plagiarism checker included in premium plan
cons: AI generative features require Premium subscription
Occasionally over-corrects discipline-specific terminology
products.verdict: The most seamless writing enhancement tool. Its browser integration means every email, paper draft, and peer review gets automatic polish.

products.name: Claude Pro
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with limited daily messages; Pro unlocks extended usage and priority access
pros: Exceptional at nuanced academic writing with minimal hallucination
200K token context window handles entire papers and datasets
Strong reasoning for complex research questions and data analysis
Projects feature organises research context across conversations
cons: No native web browsing or real-time information access
Usage caps on Pro tier during peak demand periods
products.verdict: The most thoughtful AI assistant for academic work. Claude's combination of long context, careful reasoning, and low hallucination rate makes it the top choice for researchers who need reliability over flash.

products.name: QuillBot
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with Standard and Fluency modes, 125-word paraphrase limit
pros: Seven paraphrasing modes that genuinely produce different outputs
Free tier covers casual use without hitting the paywall
Inline browser, Word, and Google Docs extensions
Grammar checker, summariser, and citation generator bundled in
cons: Academic Mode can subtly change discipline-specific terminology
Citation generator unreliable on edited volumes and pre-prints
products.verdict: The most polished paraphrasing tool on the market. Useful as a revision assistant rather than a primary drafting tool — used with intent it cuts hours off journal revisions.

products.name: Otter.ai
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with 300 transcription minutes per month, 30 min per session
products.useCase: Interview transcription, lecture capture, meeting notes
pros: Real-time transcription accurate enough for verbatim research interviews
Speaker identification automatically separates multi-participant recordings
Generous free tier suitable for occasional qualitative research
Live integrations with Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams
cons: Accent and technical-vocabulary handling weaker than human transcription
Free tier capped at 30-minute sessions — limiting for longer interviews
products.verdict: The fastest path from a recorded interview, lecture, or focus group to a searchable text transcript. Saves qualitative researchers and lecturers hours of work per week.

products.name: Scite.ai
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with limited Smart Citation lookups and basic search
pros: Smart Citations classify whether each citation supports, contrasts, or merely mentions a finding
1.2B+ citation statements indexed across 200M+ scholarly sources
Reveals replication and contradiction patterns invisible to keyword search
Assistant chat layer summarises evidence with grounded, linkable citations
cons: Premium subscription is the most expensive in the academic AI category
Coverage skews toward biomedical and STEM literature
products.verdict: An indispensable tool for serious literature work. Scite shows you which citations support a claim and which dispute it — context no other database surfaces.

products.name: Perplexity Pro
products.freeTierNote: Free plan with limited Pro searches per day; Pro unlocks full models and follow-ups
pros: Every answer ships with inline source citations you can click and verify
Academic-focused search mode prioritises peer-reviewed sources
Switch between GPT-4, Claude, Sonar, and Gemini models on Pro
Follow-up question chaining makes literature exploration genuinely fast
cons: Web-scoped — does not have native database access like Consensus or Elicit
Citation quality varies; always verify before quoting in published work
products.verdict: The best AI answer engine for researchers. Combines live web search with structured citations and is the fastest tool for the early exploratory phase of any research question.

products.name: Submagic
products.freeTierNote: Free plan covers 3 videos a month (with a watermark); paid plans from $12/mo billed yearly remove it and add length
products.useCase: Captioned clips, lecture and talk highlights, science communication
pros: Auto-generates accurate, styled captions in seconds — strong for accessibility and silent-scroll social feeds
Magic Clips pulls the best short segments out of a long lecture or talk automatically
B-roll, auto-zoom, and translation make a recorded talk look produced without an editor
Genuinely fast learning curve — usable on day one with no video-editing background
cons: Built for creators and marketers, not academics — the academic use case is real but secondary
Free plan is limited to 3 short, watermarked videos a month
Caption accuracy still needs a proofread for technical terms, names, and equations
products.verdict: The fastest way to turn a lecture, talk, or research explainer into a captioned clip people will actually watch. A creator tool at heart, but a genuinely useful one for academics doing science communication.

products.name: Everneed AI
products.freeTierNote: Free account with limited one-time credits to trial the platform — not an ongoing free tier
products.useCase: Bulk content drafting, social copy, marketing assets
pros: All-in-one: article writing, social copy, digital art, code help, and speech-to-text under one login and one bill
32 templates cover common content jobs (blog posts, ad copy, product descriptions, video scripts) so you start from a prompt, not a blank page
Low entry price — $9.99/mo or a one-time credit pack — undercuts buying separate writing, image, and transcription subscriptions
Genuinely fast for high-volume, repeatable content where speed matters more than nuance
cons: Built for marketers and entrepreneurs, not researchers — no citation handling, source grounding, or academic tone control
A wrapper over general models, so output still needs fact-checking and editing; originality and depth are the weak points
Strict no-refund policy on subscriptions and credit packs — trial the free credits before committing
products.verdict: A cheap, all-in-one content suite that earns its place for high-volume marketing copy — but it is a generalist built for creators and marketers, not a research tool. For academic writing a focused, citation-aware tool will serve you better; for fast first drafts of non-scholarly content, it is a reasonable budget pick.
